text.p: Kenneth Eriksson achieved his second world championship victory on home soil in three years on Monday when he won the Swedish Rally with a thrilling surge on the final day.

Eriksson, in a Subaru Impreza for the first time, finished 16 seconds clear of overnight leader Carlos Sainz of Spain, driving a Ford Escort, after an attack which enabled him to go clear on the opening stage of the third leg at Bjalverud.
Sainz, who has never won the Swedish event, had led by 12 seconds but was unable to resist Eriksson's speed when they restarted.
The result meant that Eriksson preserved the rally's unusual record of never having been won by a non-Scandinavian driver -- a fact which seemed to please him as much as his victory.

"Of course, it is fantastic to win on home soil again and in my first outing for Subaru," he said. "I think tyres were the decisive factor for us as every time the leader board changed during the rally it was because of tyre choice.
"I think the weather suited us better today because it was colder and it is great to win."
Sainz took a narrow lead in the world drivers' championship after the opening two rounds. He now has 12 points to 10 for Eriksson and Monte Carlo winner Italian Piero Liatti.
Reigning champion Makinen, driving a Mitsubishi Lancer, finished third as he did in the Monte, 26 seconds behind Eriksson.

He was five seconds ahead of Briton Colin McRae, in another Subaru. McRae's last-day effort was upset by two spins on the second stage of the morning. Despite finishing second in the final stage, he had to settle for fourth.

Eriksson took command after starting the day with a record-shattering effort on stage 21 when he trimmed Stig Blomqvist's five-year-old record by 13 seconds. This put him in front and he remained there for the rest of a tricky day, with most of the stages run on a mixture of gravel and ice.
The result strengthened Subaru's position at the top of the manufacturers' world championship. They have now won both rallies this year and have 23 points to Ford's 16.
